title: Notation
body_md: We use bold lowercase and uppercase letters to denote vectors and matrices, respectively; the superscripts $(\cdot)^T$ and $(\cdot)^\dag$ stand for the transpose and Hermitian transpose, respectively; ${ \textbf{I} }_{N}$ denotes an $N\times N$ identity matrix; $\boldsymbol{0}_{N \times K}$ denotes the $N \times K$ zero matrix; ${\bf a}_j$ denotes the $j$th element of vector ${\bf a}$; $\mathrm{tr}(\cdot)$ and $(\cdot)^{-1}$ denote the trace operator and matrix inverse, while $\mathrm{diag}(\cdot)$ constructs a diagonal matrix from its vector argument; $\Vert\cdot\Vert_2$ denotes the Euclidean vector norm and matrix spectral norm; $\|\mathbf{A}\|_\mathrm{F}^2$ denotes the squared Frobenius norm of matrix $\mathbf{A}$;  $\Im\{\cdot\}$, $\Re\{\cdot\}$, and $\angle(\cdot)$ are the imaginary component, real component, and the argument of the complex-valued argument, respectively; $\rm{atan2}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denotes the four-quadrant inverse tangent of two inputs; a circularly symmetric complex Gaussian random variable with variance $\sigma^2$ is denoted by $\mathcal{CN}(0,\sigma^2)$; Finally, $\mathbb{E}\{\cdot\}$ denotes the statistical expectation.
